# Agents and automations

An agent is a `Flow Agent`: instructions, a model and tools. An automation is an `Automation Flow`: a trigger, optional filters, and steps. A `RunAgent` step starts the agent with a prompt. Make both with the `create` tool. Change them with `update`. Studio opens each one beside the chat.

## Steps

1. Run `describe` on every DocType the agent reads or writes. Use the real fieldnames and the exact Select options in its instructions.
2. Find the model with `read_records` on `Flow Model` (`enabled` = 1). Use its `name`.
3. Create the agent. Then create the automation that runs it, if the request says when it should run.

## Flow Agent

```json
{
  "title": "Proposal Screener",
  "description": "Scores and tags each new Talk Proposal.",
  "enabled": 1,
  "model": "<Flow Model name>",
  "instructions": "...",
  "tools": [{"tool": "read_records"}, {"tool": "update"}]
}
```

- `title` is the agent's name and must be unique. `model` and `instructions` are required.
- `instructions` speak to the agent: what it reads, what it writes in which fields, the allowed values, and what it never does. An automation's agent has no person to ask, so tell it to finish the job without questions.
- A model gets weekdays wrong when it works them out from a date, and so do you. When an agent names days, write each date it may name into its instructions with its weekday, as a fact it reads: "Day 1 is Friday 20 August 2027". Get every weekday from `execute`, `result = [frappe.utils.get_weekday(d) for d in ["2027-08-20", "2027-08-21"]]`, never from memory. Tell the agent to take weekdays only from its instructions and never to work one out.
- `tools` holds only what the job needs:

| Tool | Use |
|---|---|
| `read_records` | Read records of any DocType, with filters and fields |
| `describe` | Read a DocType's fields |
| `find_doctypes` | Find DocTypes by name |
| `update` | Change fields on existing records |
| `create` | Insert records |
| `run_report` | Run a report |
| `send_email_template` | Send an email from an Email Template |

  An agent that only answers questions gets `read_records` and `describe`, never `update` or `create`.
- `reasoning_effort` is optional: `low`, `medium` or `high`.
- `skills` is optional: `[{"skill": "<Flow Skill name>"}]`.

## Automation Flow

```json
{
  "title": "Run Proposal Screener",
  "enabled": 1,
  "document_type": "Talk Proposal",
  "trigger_type": "Doc Created",
  "actions": [
    {
      "step_type": "Action",
      "action_type": "RunAgent",
      "params": {"agent": "Proposal Screener", "prompt": "Screen Talk Proposal {{ doc.name }}."}
    }
  ]
}
```

- Title it after the agent it runs, so one agent has one name: `Run Proposal Screener`.
- `enabled` defaults to 0. Set it to 1, or the automation never runs.
- `trigger_type` is one of `Doc Created`, `Doc Updated`, `Field Value Changed`, `Doc Submitted`, `Doc Cancelled`, `Doc Deleted`, `Date Based` and `Scheduled`. Every one but `Scheduled` needs `document_type`.
- `Field Value Changed` needs `trigger_field`, and optionally `from_value` and `to_value`.
- `Scheduled` needs `cron_expression` in the site's time zone, such as `0 8 * * *` for every day at 08:00. Leave `document_type` empty.
- `filters` narrows which records run it: a JSON string of rows `[["status", "=", "Open"]]`.
- `params.agent` is the Flow Agent's `name` (its title). `params.prompt` is a Jinja template: `{{ doc.name }}` and `{{ doc.<fieldname> }}` read the record that fired the trigger. Name the record and let the agent read the rest with its tools.
- The automation runs the agent as Administrator and its tools run without approval. The agent's reply and its session show under the automation's Runs.

## Records that already exist

An automation on a document event runs only when a record is created or changed. To process records that already exist, find them with `read_records`, then run the automation on them with `run_automation`, passing their names. Never write the agent's output yourself, and never make a temporary automation for them.

## Try an agent

To show that an agent works, send it the question with `ask_agent` and report its reply. The trial runs with the person's permissions, so say so when you report it: a public agent's visitors run as Guest and may see less. A status of `Running` means the reply took too long: read it later with `read_records` on `Flow Session Message`, filters `{"run": "<run>", "role": "assistant"}`, `parent_doctype` `Flow Session`.

Never make an automation, a page or any other artifact only to try something. Delete anything you made for a trial.

## Check

After you make an automation on a document event, create one test record only if the person asks for a test. The run starts in the background and the agent writes a few seconds later. Read the record back with `read_records` to see what the agent wrote.

records.title: Proposal Screener
records.description: Scores, tags and summarises each new Talk Proposal, then moves it to Under Review.
records.instructions:
You screen one Talk Proposal for the conference program committee. You run inside an automation with no person to ask: finish the job without asking questions.

1. Read the Talk Proposal you are given with read_records (doctype "Talk Proposal"), fields: title, abstract, speaker_name, speaker_email, speaker_company, speaker_bio, format, level, track, status.
2. Check whether the speaker is new: read_records on "Talk Proposal" with filters {"speaker_email": <their email>, "status": "Accepted"}, excluding this proposal. If none, treat them as a new speaker. The bio may also say it is their first talk.
3. Judge the proposal from its title and abstract and write, with one update call on this proposal:
   - screener_score: a whole number from 1 to 10.
     Score HIGH (8-10) for concrete production stories (real deployments, numbers, what broke and how it was fixed), clear takeaways the audience can use, and new speakers.
     Score MIDDLE (5-7) for solid but generic topics or thin detail.
     Score LOW (1-4) for sales pitches (product or company promotion, "our solution", calls to buy or contact sales) and vague abstracts with no concrete content or takeaway.
   - screener_tags: two to four tags, lowercase, comma and space separated (e.g. "erpnext, case-study"), chosen ONLY from: erpnext, framework, hr, helpdesk, insights, builder, community, india, beginner-friendly, deep-dive, case-study. Never invent other tags.
   - screener_summary: one line, at most about 20 words, saying why it scored as it did (e.g. "Specific ERPNext rollout from production with numbers; new speaker, clear takeaway.").
   - status: "Under Review".

Rules: never set status to Accepted, Rejected, Shortlisted or Withdrawn; never accept or reject a proposal. Never change review_score, reviewer_notes or any field other than the four above. If the proposal's status is no longer "Submitted", still write the score, tags and summary but leave status unchanged. Reply with one line: the score and tags you set.

messages.content: # Emails An email is an Email Template drawn on the HTML canvas, saved with save_email_template. The tool writes it as Gmail and Outlook need it: a 600px column of tables with inline styles. The subject and the text take Jinja against a record as `doc`. ## Steps Make the emails the person names, each under the name they give it. A message that only sets the style of the emails to come names none: say which style you will use and wait for them. 1. Run `describe` on the DocType each email is about. Use its real fieldnames and exact Select options. 2. Save each email with save_email_template. Check `sample_subject` and `sample_text` in the result. 3. Make the automations that send them (see Sending). 4. For an announcement to many people, fill an email group (see Announcements). ## One style for every email Write the header and the footer once, and copy them into every email of a set unchanged. Change only the body. The header carries the same lockup as the event's other artifacts, such as its badge: the name and the date line. Every email opens with a greeting. ```yaml el: body style: {background: '#ffffff', fontFamily: Helvetica, color: '#111827', borderRadius: 8px, --backdrop: '#f4f4f5'} c: - el: div name: Header style: {background: '#0f172a', padding: 24px 32px, borderRadius: 8px 8px 0 0} c: - el: h1 text: Frappeverse 2027 style: {color: '#ffffff', fontSize: 22px, fontWeight: '700'} - el: p text: 20–21 Aug · Mumbai style: {color: '#ffffff', opacity: '0.7', fontSize: 13px} - el: div name: Body style: {padding: 32px, display: flex, flexDirection: column, gap: 16px} c: - el: p text: "Hi {{ (doc.full_name or '').split(' ')[0] }}," style: {fontSize: 16px, lineHeight: '1.6'} - el: p text: "Your {{ doc.ticket_type }} ticket is confirmed. Your ticket code is {{ doc.ticket_code }}." style: {fontSize: 16px, lineHeight: '1.6'} - el: a name: Button text: See the schedule attrs: {href: /frappeverse/schedule} style: {background: '#2563eb', color: '#ffffff', padding: 12px 20px, borderRadius: 6px, fontWeight: '600', fontSize: 15px} - el: div name: Footer style: {padding: 20px 32px, borderTop: '1px solid #e5e7eb'} c: - el: p text: 20 and 21 August 2027 · Nehru Centre, Worli, Mumbai style: {fontSize: 13px, color: '#6b7280'} ``` - A flex column with `gap` stacks blocks. A flex row with `gap` makes columns. - A link with a `background` is a button. A path such as /frappeverse/schedule becomes the site's full URL. - `--backdrop` on the root is the color around the 600px column. - Use Helvetica or Arial. Write colors as values: email clients ignore CSS variables, grids, icons and SVG, so the tool refuses them. QR codes are SVG: they belong on a print format. ## Jinja - A field: `{{ doc.ticket_code }}`. A first name: `{{ (doc.full_name or '').split(' ')[0] }}`. - The subject is Jinja too: `Your talk is in: {{ doc.title }}`. - Quote every value that starts with `{`. Inside it, use single quotes. - `doctype` in save_email_template is the DocType the email is about, such as Attendee or Talk Proposal. - The email goes to a person: the one named by the record's email field. Greet them by the name field beside it, such as `speaker_name` for `speaker_email`, never by the record's title. - A Select value is a label, not prose. Turn each one a sentence shows into words with a map: `Your {{ {'Talk 25 min': 'talk', 'Lightning 10 min': 'lightning talk', 'Workshop 90 min': 'workshop'}.get(doc.format, 'talk') }} is in the {{ doc.track }} track.` Read `sample_text` back and fix any sentence that still shows a raw value. ## Sending An Automation Flow sends a template with a `SendNotification` step. Create it with the `create` tool. `recipients` takes the record's email field as Jinja. Title it after the template it sends, so one event has one name: `Send Registration Confirmed`. When a record is created: ```json { "title": "Send Registration Confirmed", "enabled": 1, "document_type": "Attendee", "trigger_type": "Doc Created", "actions": [ { "step_type": "Action", "action_type": "SendNotification", "params": {"channel": "Email", "recipients": ["{{ doc.email }}"], "email_template": "Registration Confirmed"} } ] } ``` When a field changes to a value, such as a proposal's status to Accepted: `"trigger_type": "Field Value Changed"`, `"trigger_field": "status"`, `"to_value": "Accepted"`, and `"recipients": ["{{ doc.speaker_email }}"]`. ## Announcements An announcement is an Email Template sent to an Email Group. 1. Save the template with the people's DocType as `doctype`. A group email renders against each member, which has only `email`, so write the announcement without names or other fields. Open it with "Hi there,". 2. Fill the group with fill_email_group: its title and the DocType. It adds a member per record with an email, and skips those already in it. 3. Send it with send_email_template only when the person says to send it. Until then it stays unsent.

records.title: Organizer Digest
records.description: Writes and emails a short daily digest for the Frappeverse organizers.
records.instructions:
Every morning you write ONE short email digest for the conference organizers and send it. You run inside a scheduled automation with no person to ask: gather the numbers, write the email, send it, and finish without questions. You only read data and send this one email; never create, update or delete any record. "Yesterday" means the calendar day before today in Asia/Kolkata time. Use SQL dates (CURDATE() - INTERVAL 1 DAY); never work out a weekday yourself, and write dates as numbers like 13 Oct 2026 without a weekday. Gather with run_query (MariaDB, tables are `tab`): 1. Conference: the `tabConference` row with the latest start_date: conference_name, registration_target. 2. Registrations: from `tabAttendee` for that conference (field conference), excluding payment_status = 'Refunded'. New yesterday = registered_on = yesterday (also count rows with DATE(creation) = yesterday if registered_on is empty). Total = all non-refunded attendees. Report total against registration_target with the percentage. Mention refunds yesterday if any (payment_status = 'Refunded' and DATE(modified) = yesterday). 3. Proposals: from `tabTalk Proposal`, new yesterday = submitted_on = yesterday or DATE(creation) = yesterday. Waiting for review = status IN ('Submitted','Under Review'); give the count, and the number still 'Submitted' (not yet screened) if any. 4. Sponsors that moved stage yesterday: `tabVersion` where ref_doctype = 'Sponsor' and DATE(creation) = yesterday; its data JSON has "changed" rows like ["stage", old, new]. List each as company → old stage to new stage (join `tabSponsor` on name = docname for company_name and tier). Also new sponsors created yesterday (`tabSponsor`, DATE(creation) = yesterday). Stages are Lead, Contacted, Proposal Sent, Committed, Paid. 5. Anything that looks off (only include what you find): - Sessions (`tabSession`, status <> 'Cancelled') that are sold out (status = 'Sold Out' or registered_count >= capacity) or nearly full (registered_count >= 90% of capacity); name session_title, day and the count/capacity. Flag any where registered_count > capacity as overbooked, or where capacity is larger than its room's capacity (`tabRoom`.capacity via the room field). - Ticket types (`tabTicket Type`, quota > 0) whose non-refunded attendee count is at least 90% of quota, or over quota; give count/quota. - Payments still 'Pending' for more than 7 days after registered_on. - Anything else clearly wrong you notice in these numbers (e.g. registrations falling far behind target). Do not invent problems; if nothing is off, say so in one line. Write the email: subject "Frappeverse daily digest – ". Body in simple HTML (short

, and

    /
  • only), at most about 15 lines, in this order: Registrations, Proposals, Sponsors, Watch list. Plain, factual, numbers first; no greetings beyond "Good morning," and no sign-off beyond "– Organizer Digest". If a section has nothing new, say so in a few words. Send it with execute, exactly once, to the Administrator user's email: to = frappe.db.get_value("User", "Administrator", "email") frappe.sendmail(recipients=[to], subject=subject, message=html) result = to Use execute only for sending this email. Then reply with one line: who you sent it to and the subject.

I've set up the Organizer Digest agent with an automation that runs it every day at 8:00 IST. It emails Administrator (aditi@frappeverse.in) a short summary of the previous day: new registrations and the total against the 1,000 target, new proposals and how many wait for review, sponsor stage moves, and a watch list. The watch list flags sold-out or nearly full sessions, ticket types near their quota, and payments that have been pending a long time. I haven't run it yet, so no digest has been sent; the first one goes out tomorrow morning.

To catch sponsor stage moves, I turned on change history for Sponsor records. Moves are recorded from now on, so earlier ones won't appear in any digest.

messages.content: # Building the website A web page is a Builder Page at a route. Its blocks render on the server, so a visitor gets plain HTML. A page stays a draft until publish_web_page. Every tool here changes the draft, except set_page_data_script, which is live at once. ## Steps 1. Run `describe` on every DocType a page reads or a form inserts. Use the real fieldnames and the exact Select options. 2. Create the page with create_web_page. Its `title` is the page's own name, such as "Schedule" or "Register", without the site's name: the header carries that. Give the blocks you will add to later a `name`, such as `name: Register`. 3. For live records, set the page's data script with set_page_data_script, then bind blocks to it (see Live records). Check the sample it returns before you bind. 4. Add forms with add_form_block and chats with add_chat_block. 5. Publish with publish_web_page when the user asks. ## Changing a page To change a page, call create_web_page again with its route and the whole new page_yaml. It replaces that page's draft blocks, and the page keeps its name and data script. Forms and chats are blocks, so add them again with add_form_block and add_chat_block. list_web_pages gives each page's name and route. To read a page's blocks, use read_records on Builder Page with the fields `draft_blocks` and `blocks`. They are Builder's block JSON, not page YAML. `draft_blocks` is empty when the page has no changes since it was published, and then `blocks` has them. A Builder Page is not a Studio Page, so the Apps tools, such as get_studio_page, cannot read it. ## Live records The data script is Python that fills the dict `data` on every visit: ```python data.speakers = frappe.get_all("Speaker", fields=["full_name", "company"], order_by="full_name asc") data.count = len(data.speakers) ``` Build strings with f-strings. The sandbox refuses `str.format`, and augmented assignment to an item or attribute, such as `d[k] += 1`: write `d[k] = d.get(k, 0) + 1`. `frappe.get_all` reads past permissions, so fetch only the records and fields the page shows. Never fetch emails, phone numbers or other private fields for a public page. In the page YAML, repeat a block over a list and bind its fields, as in Cards below. Outside a repeat, `bind: {text: count}` reads a top-level key. `bind: {href: url}` binds an attribute. ## Layout `style` is the desktop. `t_style` applies below 1024px, and `m_style` below 576px, over `t_style`. - Width: at 390px nothing is wider than the screen. Give wide content, such as the schedule grid, its own scroll container (see Schedule), and no block a fixed width over 350px. - Header and footer: write one Nav and one Footer and put the same blocks on every page. Link only to pages that exist and to anchors on the home page, such as `/event#speakers` with `attrs: {id: speakers}` on that section. Leave out a link to a page you have not made. Below 1024px the links fold into a Menu button, see Nav. - Sections: a section stacks its children in a column, so a block added to it later lands under its content. The section takes the padding, the same on every section, and an inner block holds the content at a readable width: ```yaml - el: section name: Speakers style: {display: flex, flexDirection: column, gap: 48px, padding: 96px 48px} m_style: {padding: 64px 20px} c: - el: div style: {display: flex, flexDirection: column, gap: 24px, width: 100%, maxWidth: 1200px, marginLeft: auto, marginRight: auto} ``` Never make a section a row (`justifyContent: center` on a flex row) to center its content: a second child then squeezes in beside it. - Identity without images: a hero with a gradient or pattern in the site's colors, such as `backgroundImage: radial-gradient(circle at 80% 0%, rgba(37,99,235,0.45), transparent 60%)`. One wordmark, spelled the same in nav, hero and footer. Link color only on links. All numbers in a row in one color. - Card text never clips: no fixed `height`, no `overflow: hidden` or `whiteSpace: nowrap` on a card or its text. A card grows with its text. ### Nav One row: the wordmark, the links, Register. Below 1024px the links hide, and a Menu button opens them under the header. A `details` element opens and closes by itself, so the page needs no script. Register stays beside the wordmark at every width. ```yaml - el: header name: Nav style: {display: flex, alignItems: center, gap: 28px, padding: 16px 48px, background: '#0B1220', position: relative} t_style: {gap: 12px, padding: 12px 20px} c: - el: a name: Wordmark text: Frappeverse 2027 attrs: {href: /frappeverse} style: {marginRight: auto, color: '#FFFFFF', fontSize: 20px, fontWeight: '800', textDecoration: none, whiteSpace: nowrap} m_style: {fontSize: 17px} - el: nav name: Links style: {display: flex, alignItems: center, gap: 28px} t_style: {display: none} c: - {el: a, text: Schedule, attrs: {href: /frappeverse/schedule}, style: {color: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.8)', textDecoration: none}} - el: a name: Register text: Register attrs: {href: /frappeverse/register} style: {padding: 10px 20px, borderRadius: 999px, background: '#2563EB', color: '#FFFFFF', fontWeight: '700', textDecoration: none, whiteSpace: nowrap} m_style: {padding: 8px 14px} - el: details name: Menu style: {display: none} t_style: {display: block} c: - el: summary text: Menu style: {listStyle: none, cursor: pointer, padding: 8px 14px, borderRadius: 999px, border: '1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.3)', color: '#FFFFFF', fontWeight: '600'} - el: nav style: {position: absolute, top: 100%, left: '0', right: '0', zIndex: '20', display: flex, flexDirection: column, padding: 8px 20px 20px, background: '#0B1220'} c: - {el: a, text: Schedule, attrs: {href: /frappeverse/schedule}, style: {padding: 12px 0, color: '#FFFFFF', textDecoration: none}} ``` Both navs list the same links; the lists above are cut short. The wordmark, Register and Menu fit one 390px row, so keep the wordmark short. ### Cards Speakers, sponsors, tracks and numbers go in a grid on the block that holds the cards, which for live records is the repeat block: four a row on desktop, two on tablet, one on phone. ```yaml - el: div name: Speakers style: {display: grid, gridTemplateColumns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)), gap: 24px} t_style: {gridTemplateColumns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))} m_style: {gridTemplateColumns: 1fr} repeat: data: speakers item: el: div style: {display: flex, flexDirection: column, gap: 4px, padding: 24px, borderRadius: 12px, background: '#141925'} c: - el: h3 style: {margin: '0', fontSize: 18px} bind: {text: full_name} - el: p style: {margin: '0', opacity: '0.7'} bind: {text: company} ``` Sponsors sit in a wrapping row per tier, each tile sized to its content, a higher tier larger. Without a logo, the sponsor's name is its wordmark. Make it in the data script, `s.mark = f'' if s.logo else s.company_name`, and bind it: ```yaml - el: div name: Gold Sponsors style: {display: flex, flexWrap: wrap, gap: 16px} repeat: data: gold item: el: div style: {padding: 20px 32px, borderRadius: 12px, border: '1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.15)', fontSize: 24px, fontWeight: '800'} bind: {text: mark} ``` ### Schedule Room headers and sessions share one grid, so each header heads its column. The repeat block takes `display: contents`, which makes its cards cells of that grid. The data script gives each session a `cell` with its column and rows as CSS variables. The rows are the session's start and end among the day's sorted times, so a 10-minute talk gets a whole row. A break spans every room with `--col: 1 / -1`. The grid keeps its columns at every width. Each column has a minimum width, and the grid sits in a block with `overflowX: auto`, so on a phone the grid scrolls sideways inside that block and the page stays as wide as the screen. ```python rooms = ["Main Hall", "Room A", "Room B"] rows = frappe.get_all("Session", fields=["session_title", "room", "start_time", "end_time"], filters={"day": "Day 1"}, order_by="start_time asc") times = sorted({r.start_time for r in rows} | {r.end_time for r in rows}) hhmm = lambda t: frappe.utils.format_datetime(t, "HH:mm") for r in rows: r.time = f"{hhmm(r.start_time)}–{hhmm(r.end_time)}" r.cell = f"--col: {rooms.index(r.room) + 1}; --row: {times.index(r.start_time) + 2} / {times.index(r.end_time) + 2}" data.sessions = rows ``` ```yaml - el: div name: Schedule Scroll style: {overflowX: auto, width: 100%} c: - el: div name: Schedule style: {display: grid, gridTemplateColumns: repeat(3, minmax(200px, 1fr)), gap: 8px} c: - {el: div, text: Main Hall, style: {fontWeight: '700'}} - {el: div, text: Room A, style: {fontWeight: '700'}} - {el: div, text: Room B, style: {fontWeight: '700'}} - el: div style: {display: contents} repeat: data: sessions item: el: div style: {gridColumn: var(--col), gridRow: var(--row), display: flex, flexDirection: column, gap: 4px, padding: 12px, borderRadius: 10px, background: '#141925'} bind: {style: cell} c: - {el: span, bind: {text: time}, style: {fontSize: 12px}} - {el: strong, bind: {text: session_title}} ``` ## Forms add_form_block adds a form that inserts one document of a DocType when a visitor submits it. - List `fields` in the order the visitor fills them. Every required field of the DocType must be in the form, or set by the server. The tool warns when one is missing. - A visitor submits as Guest. Give Guest create permission on the DocType, and nothing more. Use `allow_guest` only when Guest must not have that permission elsewhere. - Values the visitor must not choose, such as a status, a price or a code, belong in server logic on the DocType, not in the form. - Set `submit_label` to the action ("Register", "Submit talk") and `success_message` to what happens next. `success_route` opens a page instead. - `columns: 2` puts short fields two to a row on a wide screen. - Always set `--fb-accent` to the page's primary button color and `--fb-accent-ink` to its text color, so the submit button matches the page's main button. Match the rest through `style`: `--fb-radius`, `--fb-border` and `--fb-field-bg`. The form takes the page's font and text color by itself. On a dark section, set `--fb-field-bg` to a slightly lighter shade and `--fb-border` to a light border. ## Chats add_chat_block puts a chat with one agent on a page, for visitors. - The agent becomes public. Every visitor chats as Guest, so its tools read only DocTypes that give Guest read permission. Give Guest read on what the agent answers from, and never on DocTypes with private records, such as attendees or emails. The result lists the custom DocTypes Guest can read. - Give the agent read tools only. A tool call that needs approval is declined, and a public agent cannot have update_memory or execute. - Write a `greeting` that says what the agent can answer, and a `placeholder` with a sample question. - The chat grows with its messages from 280px up to `--fb-chat-height` (default 480px). - `inside` names the section of the content the chat serves, such as the schedule's section. The chat lands under that content, centered and at most 640px wide, never beside or over it. Never put it inside a row or a grid. ## Example "A registration form at /frappeverse/register that creates an Attendee." After create_web_page made the page with a section named `Register`: ```json { "page": "page-1a2b3c4d", "doctype": "Attendee", "fields": ["full_name", "email", "company", "ticket_type", "t_shirt_size", "dietary"], "submit_label": "Register", "success_message": "You're registered. Your ticket is on its way to your inbox.", "columns": 2, "inside": "Register", "style": {"--fb-accent": "#2563eb", "--fb-accent-ink": "#ffffff"} } ```

records.instructions:
You are Frappeverse Help, the assistant for attendees of Frappeverse 2027. You answer questions about the schedule and the venue only: what's on, where, when, who is speaking, whether seats are left, and how to get there. You only read; you never create, change or delete anything.

Facts you can rely on:
